This beta brings everything planned for 2.2.0 (below). It is also the first release that can update an installed copy without asking for administrator approval, so updating from here on should not show a UAC prompt unless the Shell core itself changes.

This version also has everything from 2.1.1, including the app in Spanish.

**Tray and start with Windows**
- Closing the Nilesoft Shell Pro window now leaves the app running in the system tray, the area next to the clock. Click its icon to open the window again. Right-click it for *Open Nilesoft Shell Pro*, *Check for updates*, *Restart Explorer* and *Quit*.
- The app starts with Windows, in the tray, without opening its window. It doesn't need administrator rights, and it only applies to your Windows account.
- While it is in the tray, the app checks for updates shortly after Windows starts and then about every eight hours. When a new version is out you get a Windows notification: *Nilesoft Shell Pro 2.x is available. Click to see what's new.* Clicking it opens the app on Home, where the update banner is. If the new version changes the Shell core, the notification says that installing it needs administrator approval; the app never asks for that by itself while it is in the tray. You are told once about each version, and never about a version you skipped. *Check for updates automatically*, the *Beta* channel and *Download and install updates automatically* work as before.
- Starting the app again from the Start menu opens the window you already have, also when it is in the tray.
- In the tray the app draws nothing and uses little memory. It wakes up only for its icon and the update checks.
- *Preferences > Startup and tray* has two switches, both on by default: *Keep Nilesoft Shell Pro in the system tray* and *Start with Windows*. Turn off the first one and the app works like before: closing the window ends it, there is no tray icon, and it doesn't start with Windows.
- The app sets up starting with Windows once, the first time you run this version. If you turn it off, in the app or in Windows (*Settings > Apps > Startup* or Task Manager), it stays off.
- Uninstalling the MSI closes the app and removes the start with Windows entry. For a portable copy, turn off *Keep Nilesoft Shell Pro in the system tray* before you delete its folder.
- Docs: [Startup and tray](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/app/preferences/#startup-and-tray).

**Updates without administrator rights**
- In-app updates no longer ask for administrator approval. Most releases only change the app and the menu files that come with it; for an install for all users (the MSI), these are now installed for you alone, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Nilesoft Shell Pro`, and Program Files is left as it is. The Start menu shortcut keeps working: the installed app starts your newer copy.
- Only a release that changes the Shell core (`shell.dll` or `shell.exe`, shared by everyone on the PC) needs administrator approval. The app says so and offers *Install with administrator approval* or *Later*. Nothing asks for approval until you press that button, and automatic updates never install such a release; they only tell you about it.
- Portable copies update as before, in their own folder, without administrator rights.
- Your personal configuration gets the new menu files after an app update too, still without administrator rights. Files you edited are kept, as before.
- Home shows both versions when they differ, for example *Shell core 2.1.1 · app 2.2.0*.
- Each release now also has `NilesoftShellPro-<version>-x64-app.zip` (the app update) and `update.json` (what the release changes, with the SHA-256 of every file). Every file is checked before it is installed.

**Narrow windows**
- The app adapts to narrow windows and longer translations: buttons, settings columns and the menu preview no longer overflow or overlap.
